settings.lede: A daily vitamin jelly for busy adults: one 90 g pouch with 15 vitamins and minerals, made with real fruit. No pills to swallow, no powder to mix.

settings.title: Out the door
settings.text: Today's pouch on the walk to the train, because breakfast didn't happen.

settings.title: Between classes or calls
settings.text: Keep a box in your bag, locker or desk drawer and have one between the busy bits.

settings.title: Travel days
settings.text: A week of pouches fits in a carry-on. No powder to explain at security.

settings.title: Gym before dinner
settings.text: Forgot this morning? It's already in your gym bag.

settings.title: Night shift break
settings.text: Nurse, warehouse or overnight shift? Ten seconds, no kitchen needed.

settings.question: What is jelgo?
settings.answer: A daily vitamin jelly: one 90 g squeeze pouch with 15 vitamins and minerals. The format is everyday in Japanese convenience stores, where office workers grab one instead of a bar or a shake.

settings.question: How is it different from AG1 or IM8?
settings.answer: Greens powders pack more ingredients into one scoop, and they work well if you have time to mix them. jelgo carries 15 vitamins and minerals and needs no water, no shaker and no cleanup, so the routine survives early meetings and travel.

settings.question: Are the flavours different formulas?
settings.answer: No. All five flavours have the same 15 vitamins and minerals. Pick by taste, or rotate with the Discovery Box or the 30-Day Variety Box.

settings.question: How many should I have a day?
settings.answer: One pouch a day. A 30-pack is one month.

settings.question: Does it need the fridge?
settings.answer: No. Pouches are shelf-stable until opened and fine at room temperature. Chilled is our favourite.

settings.question: Which pack should I buy?
settings.answer: New to jelgo? Start with the Discovery Box: ten pouches, two of every flavour. Once you know your favourite, a 30-pouch pack is one month of jelgo and works out to about $1.97 a pouch.

settings.question: Is this store taking real orders?
settings.answer: Not yet. jelgo is a class project for Business 4572 at Ivey Business School, and checkout runs in test mode: no card is charged and nothing ships. To test it, pay with card 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiry 12/30 and security code 123, and leave "Save my information" unticked.

settings.question: Who is jelgo for?
settings.answer: Adults who want their daily vitamins without pills or powders: commuters, students, shift workers, parents and travellers. jelgo is made for adults 18+ and is not meant for children.

settings.question: Is it made with real fruit?
settings.answer: Yes. Every flavour is made with fruit juice concentrate and fruit purée, sweetened with fruit and erythritol, with no added sugar. The full ingredient list is on each flavour's page.

settings.name: Vitamin A
settings.role: Helps maintain eyesight, skin and immune function.
settings.more: Your body can also make vitamin A from beta-carotene, the pigment that makes carrots orange.

settings.name: Vitamin C
settings.role: An antioxidant that helps form collagen and supports immune function.
settings.more: Your body can't store much vitamin C, so it needs a little every day. One pouch covers all of it.

settings.name: Vitamin D3
settings.role: Helps the body absorb calcium for strong bones and teeth.
settings.more: Your skin makes vitamin D from sunlight, which is in short supply during a Canadian winter.

settings.name: Vitamin E
settings.role: An antioxidant that helps protect cells.
settings.more: It's fat-soluble, so it's stored in the body and works alongside vitamin C.

settings.name: Vitamin K
settings.role: Helps blood clot normally and supports bones.
settings.more: The K comes from "Koagulation", the German word for clotting.

settings.name: Thiamin (B1)
settings.role: Helps turn the carbohydrates you eat into energy.
settings.more: B vitamins dissolve in water, so the body uses what it needs and flushes the rest.

settings.name: Riboflavin (B2)
settings.more: Riboflavin is naturally bright yellow, which is why some vitamins are that colour.

settings.name: Niacin (B3)
settings.role: Helps release energy from food and maintain skin.
settings.more: Niacin is needed by hundreds of enzymes that turn food into usable energy.

settings.name: Pantothenic acid (B5)
settings.role: Helps the body use fats, carbs and protein.
settings.more: Its name comes from the Greek "pantothen", meaning "from everywhere": small amounts are in almost every food.

settings.name: Vitamin B6
settings.role: Helps form red blood cells and use protein.
settings.more: B6 helps the body make several messenger chemicals in the brain and nervous system.

settings.name: Biotin (B7)
settings.role: Helps the body use fats and protein.
settings.more: Biotin was once called vitamin H, from the German "Haar und Haut": hair and skin.

settings.name: Folate (B9)
settings.more: The name comes from the Latin "folium", meaning leaf, because it was first found in spinach.

settings.name: Vitamin B12
settings.role: Helps form red blood cells and keep nerves healthy.
settings.more: B12 is found almost only in animal foods, so many vegans get it from fortified foods or supplements.

settings.name: Zinc
settings.role: Supports immune function and normal growth.
settings.more: The body has no special store for zinc, so a steady daily supply matters.

settings.name: Magnesium
settings.role: Helps muscles and nerves work and maintains bones.
settings.more: Magnesium takes part in hundreds of reactions in the body. One pouch covers a starting share, and food does the rest.

settings.intro: Built around Canadian daily values for adults. Tap any card to see where else it is found and how much one pouch covers.
